subject: Aurora - token velocity, streaming requirements & SLO check-in
messages:
From: nikhil_sharma
To: Saira Khan <saira.khan@aurorahealth.com>, Evan Liu <evan.liu@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel, ben_carter
Date: 2027-11-09T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Aurora - token velocity, streaming requirements & SLO check-in

Hi Saira / Evan — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can size a pilot and draft an SLA: 

1) Goals from your side
- Real-time summarization and decisioning on clinical notes (non-PII extracts)
- Live partial-transcript streaming for clinician dictation during peak hours

2) SLOs discussed (please confirm):
- Non-streaming generation: p95 latency target ~200ms for single-shot calls, p99 < 500ms (soft)
- Streaming segments: end-to-end partial transcript delivery p95 < 400ms

3) Workload numbers we need to finalize sizing (please confirm exacts):
- Steady-state QPS (single-shot inference): 8 qps
- Peak burst QPS: ~320 qps for short windows (30–90s) every ~6 hours
- Typical tokens per non-stream request (median): ~800 tokens; 95th-percentile up to 3,500
- Streaming: ~50 concurrent streaming connections during peaks, average token emission ~10 tokens/sec/connection

4) Security/ops asks
- Will need to confirm retention window and KMS key details for the pilot
- Any compliance docs (SOC2, DPA) we should share up front?

Next steps proposed from Redwood:
- We’ll produce a first-pass sizing estimate and proposed Dedicated baseline + burst pool to handle your peaks.
- Request: please share a 24-hour sample traffic CSV (columns: timestamp, tokens, is_streaming) and your preferred monthly token budget so we can run a cost estimate.

I’ve attached an intake CSV template and a one-pager on pilot scope. I’ll loop in Monica and Ben for the sizing math and a proposed pilot timeline.

Thanks — Nikhil

--
Nikhil Sharma
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: aurora_workload_snapshot.csv (intake template), pilot_scope_sla.pdf

From: Saira Khan <saira.khan@aurorahealth.com>
To: nikhil_sharma
Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@aurorahealth.com>, monica_patel, ben_carter
Date: 2027-11-10T09:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Aurora - token velocity, streaming requirements & SLO check-in

Thanks Nikhil — this matches what we discussed. A few clarifications/confirmations from our side: 

- Steady-state: 8 qps (weekdays business hours), monthly average expected ~700k requests/month for this pilot feed.
- Peaks: bursts up to ~320 qps that last ~45–60s, typically tied to shift-change and nightly batch windows.
- Tokens: median ~820, mean ~1,100, 95th ~3,200. Worst-case episodic requests up to ~8,000 (rare).
- Streaming: we expect about 50 concurrent streaming sessions during peaks; each connection emits ~8–12 tokens/sec (roughly 10 tokens/sec avg). We need the streaming p95 to be within ~350–450ms for partial transcript segments.
- Latency: enterprise goal is p95 non-streaming ~200ms; we can accept p99 up to ~600ms during sustained infra issues.

Security: we can share KMS details once we have an NDA in place. We have SOC2 Type II and can provide a redacted report.

We’ll attach a 24-hour sample export of production-like traffic (anonymized). Expect it by EOD tomorrow.

If you can provide a preliminary sizing by Thursday that would help our infra review.

— Saira
Clinical AI Program Manager, Aurora Health

From: monica_patel
To: nikhil_sharma, ben_carter
Date: 2027-11-10T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Aurora sizing inputs (draft math)

Putting together rough capacity numbers based on Saira's confirmed traffic: 

Assumptions (to validate):
- Steady: 8 qps * 820 tokens/request ≈ 6,560 tokens/sec sustained
- Peak: 320 qps * 820 tokens ≈ 262,400 tokens/sec during burst windows (~45–60s)
- Streaming: 50 conns * 10 tokens/sec ≈ 500 tokens/sec additional sustained during peak windows

Notes: 
- The peak token/sec number is large but very short; we should support bursts with a dedicated burst pool (short-lived GPU capacity) and autoscaling rules capped to X GPUs for 2–3 minutes.
- For cost and latency tradeoffs, suggest testing a 4-bit quantized variant of the model and comparing p95 latency vs float16 baseline; that can reduce token/sec throughput pressure by ~2-2.5x depending on kernel availability.
- Recommend initial pilot baseline that covers steady-state + 1.5x buffer: target baseline ~10k tokens/sec, burst pool capable of absorbing up to ~270k tokens/sec for 90s windows.

Action items for Nikhil: confirm whether 820 tokens/request is acceptable to assume for the sizing doc and whether Aurora prefers Dedicated (reserved) vs Hosted with burst credits.

— Monica
Principal Performance Ops, Redwood Inference

From: nikhil_sharma
To: Saira Khan <saira.khan@aurorahealth.com>, Evan Liu <evan.liu@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel, ben_carter
Date: 2027-11-11T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Aurora - token velocity, streaming requirements & SLO check-in

Hi Saira — thanks for the sample confirmation. Based on Monica's draft math (below) here are our proposed next steps and the numbers we’ll assume unless you push back: 

Assumed for pilot sizing (please confirm by EOD Wednesday):
- Median tokens/request: 820 (95th: 3,200)
- Steady baseline target: 10,000 tokens/sec (covers 8 qps + 1.5x buffer)
- Burst pool: capacity to handle up to 270,000 tokens/sec for 90s windows (autoscale + pre-warm policy)
- Streaming pool: reserved capacity to handle 60 concurrent streams at 10 tokens/sec (600 tokens/sec) to provide headroom
- Latency targets we’ll engineer toward: p95 <= 200ms non-streaming; p95 <= 400ms streaming segments.

Deliverables we’ll send by Thursday:
- A short Redwood sizing estimate (attached: redwood_sizing_estimate_v1.xlsx) with cost guidance for Hosted vs Dedicated and expected latency ranges by model variant.
- Pilot scope & SLA draft (attached: pilot_scope_sla.pdf).
- A small config template to capture your KMS/retention choices and any routing region constraints.

If that looks good I’ll schedule a 30-minute ops sync next week with Monica and our infra lead to agree on autoscale knobs and pre-warm behavior.

Thanks — Nikhil
